- Overestimate prices when sentiment is negative (especially strong negative sentiment), especially in early forecast windows.  
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is strongly positive, particularly after recent spikes.  
- Overshoot after sharp upward sentiment spikes; reduce forecast peak by 5–10% in subsequent periods.  
- Mean-revert forecasts when sentiment is mixed or neutral; avoid prolonged upward trends unless sentiment confirms sustained bullishness.  
- Lag in price response to sentiment: if sentiment turns negative, delay price drop by 1–2 periods; if sentiment turns positive, delay price rise by 1–2 periods.  
- Avoid overconfidence in short-term forecasts when sentiment is volatile; use 3–5 period smoothing for sentiment-driven adjustments.
